title: Account security setup wizard — wires and grooming notes
body:
Purpose / context: Quick internal reference and groomable backlog for an account-level security setup wizard that walks new org admins through the most-common production settings: role model selection, API key creation, service account provisioning, and audit-log/retention defaults. Goal is to reduce first-time misconfigurations and accelerate onboarding for Dedicated/Private customers while keeping hosted customers secure by default.

Audience: PM/UX/product-engineering pairing, solutions engineers who run onboarding, and platform SREs who own audit retention. Not a final spec — sketch + decisions + open questions.

High-level flow (4 screens + review):
  1) Welcome / quick choices (progress left rail)
     - Purpose: set expectations, surface the 3 decisions we care about: who are admins, how API keys are used, do you need service accounts for automation.
     - Wire: left nav shows steps (Welcome -> Roles -> API Keys -> Service Accounts -> Audit -> Review). Main area: two-column card: left = quick checklist, right = toggleable advanced options collapse.
     - Copy: "Configure security defaults for this organization. These can be changed later in Organization settings. Recommended for most teams: minimal admin set + short-lived API keys."

  2) Roles & RBAC templates
     - Purpose: reduce freeform role creation by providing curated templates + inline preview of privileges.
     - Wire: top: horizontal pills for "Starter", "Engineering", "Ops", "Custom". Middle: card showing a list of permissions grouped (Console, Model-serving, Billing, Keys). Each permission row has a tooltip and a sample use-case. Bottom: ability to assign users/roles now or skip and invite later.
     - Shortcuts: "Add a service account with this template" checkbox that carries selection to next screen.
     - Notes: show cost/impact warning for roles that can create dedicated capacity.

  3) API key policy builder
     - Purpose: guide admins through the safest-by-default API key settings (scopes, expiry, labels, IP restrictions).
     - Wire: big form with: name, description, scopes (multi-select), expiration (preset 1d/7d/30d/never with recommended highlighted), usage type (interactive / server), allowed origins/IPs, auto-rotation toggle. Right column: live preview curl snippet + playground link.
     - Default suggestion: generate a key with 30d expiry and rotation enabled for server keys; for interactive keys default to short-lived (1h session) + browser-origin restriction.
     - UX detail: when user picks long-lived key, show an inline risk banner describing recommended mitigations (IP allowlist, tagging).

  4) Service account quick-provision
     - Purpose: let teams create service accounts for automation with attached key rotation policy and role binding.
     - Wire: list of existing service accounts (if any) with simple CRUD actions. Primary action: "Create service account" modal with fields: name, intended-use (dropdown), attach roles (select from prior RBAC template), key management option (Redwood-managed key, Customer-managed KMS, No key - use workload identity).
     - Key rotation: slider for rotation cadence (7/30/90 days) and an option to require rotation before allowed use on Dedicated pools.
     - Edge-case: for private deployments show note about offline key delivery and HSM metadata.

  5) Audit log & retention defaults
     - Purpose: let orgs pick sensible defaults and preview the types of events captured.
     - Wire: toggles for event categories (auth, admin-ops, model-inference, billing-changes). Each toggle expands a sample event feed row (timestamp, actor, action, resource, token) to show what will be recorded. Retention options: 30/90/365/Custom with cost estimate per GB-month (back-of-envelope).
     - Integrations: Enable push to external SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) with sample webhook config.

  6) Review + apply
     - Summarize choices with inline warnings and required actions (e.g., "You chose never-expiring keys — create rotation policy before launch"). Buttons: Apply to org (makes changes) / Save draft (store in console) / Export JSON (for infra-as-code onboarding).

Wireframe micro-interactions and notes:
  - While on Roles screen, clicking a permission row opens a contextual side-panel with example API calls that would be allowed/denied. Helps devs validate before applying.
  - When creating API key, the curl preview should show how to scope the key and an automatic comment with the key label.
  - Service account modal: when choosing "Customer-managed KMS", show quick checklist for required IAM bindings (links to infra docs).
  - Audit retention slider toggles a cost estimator that updates live. Must be conservative in defaults (30d).

Open questions / decisions needed:
  - Should the wizard write audit-connector configs by default or leave them disabled? (Pros: easier for customers; Cons: unexpected egress/costs).
  - Where to store drafts? Per-user in console or per-org? Recommend per-user until they press "Apply to org". Prev discussion in CONSOLE-345.
  - Terminology: "Short-lived API key" vs "Session token" — unify across docs.
  - Admin discovery: should we scan org for admin-like accounts and suggest a curated list? (Privacy questions).

Accessibility & content guidelines:
  - All toggles must have keyboard focus order matching step flow.
  - Tooltips and example JSON must have a copy-to-clipboard button.
  - Error states: if external KMS test fails, modal must show failure code + remediation link; do not block draft save.

Backlog & next steps (MVP scope vs stretch):
  MVP (target next sprint):
    - Core 4-screen wizard (Roles, API keys, Service accounts, Audit) + Review page.
    - Predefined RBAC templates (Starter, Eng, Ops).
    - API key generator with expiry presets and curl preview.
    - Service account create/delete + Redwood-managed keys only.
    - Audit toggle (basic categories) + default 30d retention.

  Stretch (post-MVP):
    - KMS integrations (CMK, HSM) plus infra-IaC export.
    - SIEM connector built-in tests.
    - Auto-suggest admin candidates and org scan.
    - Inline guided walkthrough for first 3 admins.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
  - New org admin can complete the wizard in under 10 minutes and have working keys + one service account.
  - No default long-lived keys created without explicit confirmation.
  - Audit retention default is 30d and visible in billing estimates prior to applying changes.

Tickets / owners (starter list):
  - CONSOLE-410: RBAC templates backend (owner: Marcus Lu)
  - CONSOLE-411: API key generator & curl preview (owner: Elena Gomez)
  - CONSOLE-412: Service account create flow + key store (owner: Jamal Reed)
  - CONSOLE-413: Audit retention UI + cost estimator (owner: Aisha Patel)

Loose UX sketches (textual):
  - Left rail progress + micro-help: small help icon links to "security primer" doc.
  - Roles screen: horizontal template chips + permission matrix. Permissions grouped under collapsible headings.
  - API key screen: form with two-column: left inputs, right preview + risk banner.
  - Review page: compact summary cards with edit links that jump to the corresponding step.

Notes to reviewers:
  - This lives in shared drive as a working doc; please add inline comments for any missing constraints or edge-cases from Dedicated/Private deployments.
  - See linked Confluence for technical requirements (KMS + rotation) and GH PR for some initial backend schema.

Quick decisions logged in this doc:
  - Default audit retention = 30d (Aisha, 2025-08-20)
  - Default key expiry for server keys = 30d (consensus, 2025-08-27)

Unresolved UX nitpicks (for grooming):
  - Exact copy for risk banner when enabling never-expire keys.
  - Whether to show estimated storage costs per event type or aggregate only.

Last updated notes: added service-account KMS options for Private on 2025-09-02 after SRE sync (Jamal).
